To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Ang-(1–-7), acting on the receptor Mas, inhibits the activation of p38 mitogen-activated kinase (MAPK) and stimulates the activity of SHP-1 tyrosine phosphotase, leading to inhibition of glucose-induced protein synthesis, transforming growth factor- β1 and extracellular matrix production in proximal tubules.

In proximal tubular cell lines, angiotensins-(1–7), via the Mas receptor, inhibits glucose-stimulation of p38 mitogen-activated kinase, protein synthesis and transforming growth factor-beta1, but not of extracellular matrix proteins, suggesting that angiotensin- (1–7) is a novel regulator of glucose-stimulus signalling.
In the kidney proximal tubule Ang-(1–-7) blocks high glucose-stimulatd activation of the MAPK p38.

the role of the renin–angiotensin system in the pathophysiology of diabetic nephropathy.
the study of the effects of angiotensin 1–7 (Ang-(1– 7)) on proximal tubular epithelial cell signalling in normal and high glucose conditions.

angiotensin 1-7 is a very important peptide that is able to counteract some of the effects of high glucose in the kidney.
